decision: Decide whether a candidate model improves the release-critical task under paired evaluation.
primary_outcome: Paired task-success difference on the prespecified eligible item set, accompanied by wins, losses, ties and an uncertainty interval.
denominator: All assigned eligible items evaluated under both versions; report missing pairs and failures explicitly.
independence_unit: Independent item or shared-source cluster when multiple questions derive from one document.
quality_guardrail: Critical failure slices and latency/cost constraints; pair integrity and fixed stopping policy.
minimum_data: Item/source IDs, both version IDs, paired outcomes, missingness cause, run seed and cost/latency records.
failure_handling: Never drop one-sided failures silently. Specify failure-as-outcome or unknown-outcome treatment in advance and show missing-pair sensitivity.
release_rule: Use a prespecified paired inferential method and meaningful improvement threshold plus guardrails; planning MDE is not an observed significance test.
reversal: Effect disappears under valid pairing, critical failures worsen, or dependence invalidates the independent-item calculation.
status: PROPOSED MEASUREMENT CONTRACT; NOT AN EXECUTED DOMAIN EXPERIMENT
defense: Does low planning power invalidate eight wins and no losses?
No. That paired example has exact two-sided p=.0078125. Planning power and the observed test answer different questions.
Avoid paying for a larger evaluation or a model release without enough decision-relevant evidence, while preserving critical failure checks.
